what: The trace along Henon's family m (Celestial Mechanics 13 (1976) 267, Table I) made with the ias route from his orbit 5 (the full run of the driver, 2462 recorded points), and its comparison with his table. Equal masses, the perpendicular start of src/perp.js: u1, u2, lam, t as everywhere (t half the period). Henon's values are the ones printed in his Table I (8 decimals), typed from a scan and checked by his energy E = -1/6 and by A; five of the 45 rows (orbits 2, 3, 4, 6, 11) do not pass the energy check at 1e-7 (the printed digits give 1e-7 to 5e-7 at their small pair distances) and are not used as values (orbit 11 is compared by its lam, the zero of the rotation angle). His rows are converted to our units (masses 1, G = 1, energy -1/2 scaled to the start x = -1, lam, 1 of src/perp.js) with the steps of the conversion given in the field conversion.
conversion: time unit and velocity unit: s = 2 / (x_r - x_l); lam = -1 + 2 (x_m - x_l) / (x_r - x_l); u1 = sqrt(3) s^(-1/2) v_l, u2 = sqrt(3) s^(-1/2) v_m, t = (T / 2) s^(3/2) / sqrt(3), where x_l, x_m, x_r and v_l, v_m are the printed positions and velocities of the left, middle and right body at the start of the half period and T is his period.
corrector: the bound on t in the line search of the corrector (src/shooting.js) is relative to the predicted point, 0.3 * t < t_trial < 3 * t; before that it was relative to the t of the start of the run, and the same run stopped at lam 0.6680289 (step 223, t = 0.38965 = 0.3 * 1.29885)
commands: python tools/reclose.py JOB.json OUT.json    (50 digits; the job holds u1, u2, t from the cubic through the four recorded points nearest in lam at the lam of Henon's orbit and ref = his converted values)
node test/t-bound.test.js    (the first 174 loop steps of the same run in one process)
node tools/residual-floor.mjs OUT.json LABEL=TRACE.json:127,160,205,2460,2461,2462 --k=30 --seed=1   (the lines of TRACE.json.nodes.jsonl, line n = the nth recorded point)

stop.why_the_driver_stopped: step length below 1e-9 (lost the family) near lam=0.9999
stop.note_on_the_stability_errors: relativeStability (src/relative.js) throws "eigenvalue iteration did not converge" on 124 of the 493 points that are checked, all beyond lam 0.99577 (closest approach below 0.0043); the driver records such a point with maxMod null and a field stabilityError and goes on. The last point with a value has maxMod 1.000000000048 (step 2593, lam 0.9998765398).

end_of_the_run.what: the run follows the family towards the collision orbit at lam = 1 (the start then has bodies 2 and 3 on top of each other; Henon's table ends with the limit A to infinity there). It does not reach it: lam stops at 0.9998765398, 1.235e-04 short of 1, and the driver ends by the creep of the corrector.
end_of_the_run.reading: the closest approach falls from 4.2e-3 (step 456) to 1.2e-4; t falls to 3e-6, L* grows to 103 and T* is 1.571; lam only rises (no turning back); all 24 pieces are encounter pieces (recomputed by reg.js) with a largest row sum of the piece matrices of 3.5e5 and the corrector stalls at the residual 1e-11 with steps of 1e-9 to 1e-10 in lam, as t35 - and t44 - do; no guard trips

orbit_11.how: lam of the zero of the rotation angle theta, found and refined by huntArclength (all: true, the zero refined along the family) in the run of test/t-bound.test.js; the cubic through the four recorded points nearest in lam (inverse interpolation, steps used) is given for comparison and is only as good as the spacing of the recorded points there (0.03 in lam)

residual_floor_at_the_end.what: tools/residual-floor.mjs on the trace of this file (30 trials, seed 1): the residual F of the multiple shooting system at six accepted steps, and the change of F when every node component is moved by one unit in the last place. Three steps on the way to the end where the closest approach is still above 0.03 (the first recorded points with lam above 0.5 whose closest approach is at most 0.3, 0.1 and 0.04) and the last three recorded points.
residual_floor_at_the_end.command: node tools/residual-floor.mjs OUT.json LABEL=TRACE.json:127,160,205,2460,2461,2462 --k=30 --seed=1   (the lines of TRACE.json.nodes.jsonl, line n = the nth recorded point)
residual_floor_at_the_end.reading: before the end (closest approach 0.29 to 0.04, no encounter piece) one ulp in the nodes moves F by 7e-16 to 6e-15; at the last three steps (all 24 pieces are encounter pieces, matrix entries 9.4e4 to 1.35e5) by 2.8e-11 to 3.0e-11, which is the order of the tolerance 1e-11 and of the creep of t35 - and t44 - (there 5e-11 to 2e-10 with matrix entries 7e5 to 3e6; at t62 - without creep 2e-14 to 7e-14). The end of family m has the signature of that creep, with a matrix entry smaller by a factor of 5 or more and a change of F smaller by a factor of 2 to 5.

handover.what: the same run with --handover (--handover-dlam=5e-6 --handover-steps=20, --minutes=60): the double precision part is the trace of this file point by point (2233 points, bit-identical) up to the point where the rule fired; then tools/reclose.py of that point and tools/reclose-continue.py (50 digits, natural continuation in lam, 20 steps of +5e-6 wanted).

reclosing_of_that_point.note: the double precision point is off from the 50 digit orbit by 2.4e-9, 2.9e-8 and 8.6e-8 in u1, u2, t at this closest approach

step_of_the_driver_run.note: the tools/reclose.py process of this step ended with a file-system error ("Access is denied" on os.replace of its status file, Windows) after its 4th iteration, so that attempt has no verdict; its iterations are the same as the first four of the retry

handover.reading: the hand-over fired where P100 fell below 1e-7 (lam 0.99986952, 1.3048e-4 from the collision at lam = 1, closest approach 1.3048e-4, 7e-6 before the double precision run stopped by the creep) and the 50 digit re-closing of that point converged; the first natural step of +5e-6 in lam (4 percent of the distance to lam = 1) did not converge within the 10 updates of tools/reclose.py: the residual falls and rises (25.8, 1.4, 2.3e-4, 1.7e-2, 2.6e-6, 0.41, 5.3e-6, 1.1e-3, 6.9e-8, 1.6e-5, 3.1e-11), and u2 and t change by 2 and 6 percent over the step, so the guess (the previous orbit) is too far for the plain Newton iteration. No 50 digit step beyond the hand-over point was obtained; the closest approach reached at 50 digits is that of the re-closed hand-over point, 1.3048e-4 (its pair distance of the start 1 - lam), the same as the double precision run reached to within 1.2e-4. Nothing was changed to make the step converge (no other step length, tolerance or number of updates).
